approach:
Revision of round 1. The design keeps its shape and changes where the reviewers found faults. A new pure module `crates/athena-core/src/run/stale_text.rs` finds text that still says what the change made false. It runs in two places the decision gate already uses: `producer_loop` (once, as part of the one shared send-back) and the candidate step `check_and_verify` (closing the job before the PR, the checks and the verifier). 

What it searches for, per the findings:
- (F2) Three sources feed it. (a) The diff: a `const`/`static` whose literal changed, and claim lines the change REPLACED. (b) The accepted reading, passed as `accepted` at both call sites (`producer_loop` has it at producer.rs:302, `check_and_verify` at mod.rs:1961): `from <old> to <new>` beside a named identifier, a quoted old claim after `no longer / instead of / replaces`, and a decision id cited with a reversal word. (c) Nothing is parsed from the reading beyond those three forms.
- (F4) A claim comes only from a hunk of `git diff -U0` that has both removed and added lines. A pure deletion, a deleted function and a deleted file are never claims.
- (F3, F7) A decision is "marked" only by `amended by D<n>` / `superseded by D<n>` in its own entry, a `[[link]]` with status `superseded`, or a `[[link]]` whose `newer` entry this change adds. A decision that an older entry merely amended still stands and is reported (D156 is the older of D187, decision-links.toml:188-191).

Answers to the eight findings:
- F1: main.rs stays in the plan because criterion 5 asks for the diff of the file where each help string lives. It is one `User:` question.
- F5: every doc comment in main.rs was re-surveyed against `pub const` limits (decision 6). The Hestia `review` help joins the conversion, with `urgent` corrected to `high`.
- F6: D190 cites D187 only for what is already there (the gate runs in the loop). It claims only the new parts.
- F8: the `default 1` string is built from `Parallel::default()`. `display.rs:705` is listed as rejected with its reason.

The help strings keep D156's placeholder mechanism, extended by a generic `fill_limits` (athena-cli lib.rs) run once over the whole command tree in `cli_command()`. The change is recorded as D190 (appended, `Amends D156`, link D156 -> D190) plus one CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Hook the check at the two places the decision gate already uses: `producer_loop` (once, as a send-back, next to the gate at producer.rs:498-502) and the candidate step after the gate (new block after mod.rs:2020). One pure function serves both. Both adapters pass the accepted reading. In the loop the tree is the snapshot's own git with `snapshot.base()` and `snapshot.work_tree_tree()`. At the candidate it is `self.git` with the base and candidate commits. The pinned-run guard is not copied: the check reads no build. The nested guard is kept.
decisions.reason: This is the existing shape for a finding that must reach the producer inside its loop and still stop a job before the verifier (checks.rs:734 `unreconciled_in_snapshot` and checks.rs:697 `unreconciled_decisions`, called at producer.rs:498 and mod.rs:2013). It uses `Athena::failure`, the `recorded_checks.is_none()` and `nested.is_none()` guards, and the not-an-environment-stop closing (`StopCause::of`, disk.rs:462, gives Work for any reason without the environment prefix). The pin guard exists in `run_loop_checks` (checks.rs:450) because a pinned run cannot build; this check builds nothing. The nested guard exists because the outer job sees the combined change.

rejected.option: Run it only inside `run_loop_checks` (checks.rs:444)
rejected.why: That run is advisory and is skipped for low disk, a busy slot, tool configuration and a pinned run (checks.rs:450-464). A skipped run would let stale text reach the verdict.

rejected.option: Run it only at the candidate
rejected.why: The producer would see the list only on a retry. The request asks for the list inside the producer's own loop.

rejected.option: Add it to the verifier's gap list
rejected.why: The verifier's judgement is model-based. That would make the rule prose, against the mechanism default.

decisions.choice: Detection sources (answers F2). (1) Diff values: in one file, a removed and an added `const`/`static NAME: T = LIT;` with the same NAME and different single literals (one number or one string). Old value `LIT`; keywords are the lowercase parts of NAME minus a GENERIC list (max, min, limit, default, value, count, number, size, total). (2) Reading values: a sentence of the accepted reading (summary, assumptions, criteria; split at `. `, `; ` and newlines) with `from <old> to <new>` AND a named identifier in the same sentence (SCREAMING_SNAKE, or backticked without `/` or `.`). Keywords come from that identifier. (3) Reading claims: a quoted or backticked span of at least 6 words within 40 characters after `no longer`, `instead of`, `rather than`, `replaces`, `reverses` or `used to say`. (4) Reading decisions: a sentence that holds `D<nn>` and one of reverse(s/d), supersede(s/d), overturn(s), replace(s), `no longer`. It is reported only when that heading exists in the log and the entry is not marked (decision 3). (5) Diff claims: from replaced hunks only (decision 4). A value hit is a line of a searched file that holds the old value as a whole token, shares a keyword, and does not hold the new value. A claim hit is the claim's words (case, punctuation and line wraps ignored) as a contiguous run in a searched file. A line that the diff added at the same path is never reported. If there are no needles at all, the tree is not read.
decisions.reason: The request says 'a job's reading or diff', and the accepted reading's assumption says old values come 'from removed diff lines ... and from decision-style claims in the reading'. The reading is available at both call sites (producer.rs:302; mod.rs:1961 `accepted`). Requiring a named identifier in a `from X to Y` sentence keeps this job's own criteria text ('a constant changes from 8 to 16') from becoming a needle: it has no SCREAMING_SNAKE or backticked identifier, and a bare path such as `stale_text.rs` is excluded. Reading forms (3) and (4) use markers the reader's own prose uses and name no token that is not stated.

rejected.option: Ignore the reading (the round 1 plan)
rejected.why: A job whose reading reverses a rule but whose diff removes no repeating comment would find nothing. The round 1 reason, 'not available at the candidate step', was false: `check_and_verify` receives `accepted`.

rejected.option: Take every number of the reading as an old value
rejected.why: Most numbers in a reading are criteria counts and file sizes; the check would refuse jobs that changed no limit.

rejected.option: Search the log for every decision id the reading names
rejected.why: Most citations are 'follows D156', not a reversal. A reversal word in the same sentence is required.

decisions.choice: 'Marked' (answers F3 and F7). A decision entry (from its `## D<n> ` heading to the next `## ` heading) is marked when: (a) its text holds `amended by D<nn>` or `superseded by D<nn>`, any case (the phrase form that `athena_data::decision_links::parse_supersessions` reads, with an id of at least two digits; 'amended by hand' marks nothing); or (b) the new `docs/decision-links.toml` has a `[[link]]` with `older` = the id and `status = "superseded"`; or (c) it has a `[[link]]` with `older` = the id whose `newer` heading is not in the base log (this change reconciles it itself). A link whose `newer` already stood at the base and whose status is `amended` marks nothing, because that header says the older decision 'stays active' (decision-links.toml:5-6). Outside the log, a blank-line paragraph is marked when it holds the same phrase followed by a `D<nn>` id, a backticked name or a path with an extension. The status is read with `toml_edit::DocumentMut` (a dependency of athena-core, already used at admission.rs:77), because `link_pairs` (decision_links.rs:101) drops the status. A links text that does not parse marks nothing, so the check errs toward reporting. CHANGELOG.md, `records/`, `target/` and `.git/` are never searched.
decisions.reason: The brief's exemption is 'marked amended by or superseded by'. The links list is how this repo records a supersession: of 29 `[[link]]` tables, one has status superseded and 28 amended, and only 4 'superseded by' phrases appear in the log. Counting any `older` id (round 1) would exempt D08 and D156, the two decisions that motivated this job, because D157/D160/D171 amend D08 and D187 amends D156. Rule (c) is the reconcile route the gate already teaches in its message (checks.rs:94-97: `Amends <id> in prose only` plus a link).

rejected.option: Any `older` id of any link is marked (round 1)
rejected.why: It never reports a contradiction of D08 or D156, the cases this check exists for.

rejected.option: Count the bare words 'amended by' anywhere in the entry
rejected.why: Prose such as 'the list is amended by hand' would exempt a whole entry.

rejected.option: Reuse `link_pairs` for the marks
rejected.why: It returns pairs without status, so 'amended and still standing' cannot be told from 'superseded'.

decisions.choice: Claims come only from lines the change replaces (answers F4). Hunks are read with `git diff -U0 --no-color --no-renames --no-ext-diff <from> <to>`, through the public `Git::run_bytes` (athena-git lib.rs:259; `added_lines` at lib.rs:642 uses the same command). A hunk with both removed and added lines is a replacement. A hunk with only removed lines (a deleted function, a deleted paragraph, a deleted file whose `+++` is `/dev/null`) yields no claim. A removed line must be 6 or more words (MIN_CLAIM_WORDS) and a comment or prose line (`//`, `///`, `//!`, `#` in toml, a non-table line of `.md`). It must not re-appear as an added line anywhere in the diff, so a moved comment is quiet. The finding text tells the producer the honest escape for a false hit in an old decision: add an entry that says `Amends D<n> in prose only` with an `amended` link (the convention in checks.rs:94-97 and D157). D190's Tradeoff says that claim hits are textual and may need that entry.
decisions.reason: A deleted function or file is not a reversed claim, and a hard failure after one send-back would force a bogus entry. D187 rejected failing a job on a similar heuristic (decisions.md:5502-5503). Replacement hunks are what an edit of a stated behaviour looks like in a diff, and `-U0` hunks give that pairing without writing a diff algorithm.

rejected.option: Every removed comment or prose line is a claim (round 1)
rejected.why: Deleting a function or file would fail any job that leaves a copy of its comment elsewhere.

rejected.option: Keep claim-only hits as send-back-only and close the job only on value hits and reading claims
rejected.why: Replacement-only claims with a whole-line, 6-word match are narrow enough to close on. It would leave the deliverable 'fail the check' unmet for the motivating decision case.

rejected.option: A line-level LCS diff inside the module
rejected.why: New algorithm and new tests; `git diff -U0` already gives the hunks.

decisions.choice: Exits of the new stage, one line each. PASS (no findings): the adapter returns empty (producer.rs next to :498; new block after mod.rs:2020 falls through); the loop's all-clear test (producer.rs:545-556) gains `stale.is_empty()`; no state is left; the verifier path reads next. FAIL with a send-back left: `send_backs += 1` (producer.rs:676-677), the line `stale text left where the change makes it false: <n> place(s)` joins `problems` (:557-613), `append_stale_text` adds the section to `attempt_brief` last (:701-712); the brief is the state, read by the next producer pass, which reruns the check. FAIL at the limit: the `send_backs >= PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` branch (:635-675) prints `producer   stale text still left after the send-back; the job ends before the verifier` and breaks with the report; the list is not added to `report_problems` (:583); the work tree keeps the text, which the candidate step reads next. FAIL at the candidate: the new block after mod.rs:2020 sets `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &reason)` with the reason `stale text left by the change: <list>`, keeping `changed_paths` and `verification_passed = None` as at mod.rs:2014-2018, and returns; a Failed outcome is the state; close and the records read it, and `athena retry` starts a fresh producer whose loop reruns the check. ERROR (diff, tree or blob read fails): both adapters return empty and print `producer   stale text not checked: <why>`, the policy of `settle_loop_checks` (checks.rs:432-441) that an advisory read failure never discards finished work; no state is left. HOLD: cannot happen; the check takes no slot and reads no disk gate. INTERRUPT: cannot happen inside the check (bounded git reads, no agent or process wait); the kill switch is read by the producer invocation before it and by `refuse_if_stopped` at the next stage. SKIPPED without a line: `self.nested.is_some()`, an empty change list, `recorded_checks.is_some()` (a resume at the verifier stage), no base commit in the snapshot, and no needles.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for every exit of a new stage. Each row names the file:line that handles it, the state it leaves and the code that reads that state next.

rejected.option: Treat a read error as a finding
rejected.why: A git read failure says nothing about the work; it would fail jobs for the environment.

decisions.choice: Help strings (answers F5 and F8). A re-survey of every doc comment, `after_help` and arg help in main.rs (lines 20-620, read in full) against `pub const` limits gives these conversions, each to a `{placeholder}` in the derive text, filled by `athena_cli::fill_limits(Cli::command(), &limits())` in `cli_command()` over the whole command tree (about, long about, after_help, and each arg's help): (1) `plan` main.rs:350-355 'default 3 urgent, 10 high' <- `DEFAULT_URGENT_CAP`, `DEFAULT_HIGH_CAP` (config.rs:54,56); 'one dispatch in three' <- `IMPROVEMENT_GAP + 1` (plan.rs:466); 'three or more distinct jobs' <- `REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS` (plan.rs:471). (2) `drain` after_help main.rs:321 'at most two other items' <- `IMPROVEMENT_GAP`; :323 'three or more distinct jobs' <- `REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS`; :295 'two attempts that did not land' <- `athena_core::scope_guard::HOLD_ATTEMPTS` (scope_guard.rs:80); :307 'default 1' <- `athena_data::config::Parallel::default().max_concurrency` (pub Default, config.rs:291-297; `default_max_concurrency` is private, config.rs:286); the `{ceiling}` fill stays. (3) `check` main.rs:487 'pending for 15 minutes' <- `athena_gate::attribution::PENDING_WINDOW` (attribution.rs:52). (4) Hestia `review` main.rs:573-574 'The five highest-ranked causes ... are urgent' <- `athena_core::hestia::BACKFILL_HIGH` (hestia.rs:1494), with 'urgent' corrected to 'high' as the constant's doc (hestia.rs:1492-1493), the use at hestia.rs:1924 and the module doc at hestia.rs:44 say. (5) `audience` main.rs:147 'A rating of 2 or lower' <- `athena_core::audience::LOW_RATING` (audience.rs:37). (6) Rating '1 to 5' at main.rs:147, 336 and 400 <- `athena_data::records::RATING_RANGE` (records/work.rs:181); the two `value_parser!(u8).range(1..=5)` at main.rs:337 and 401 become one `rating_parser()` that reads the same constant, so help and parser cannot drift. Spelled numbers become digits. Not converted, each with its reason: 'every 30 seconds' (main.rs:370) is a literal `Duration::from_secs(30)` in drain.rs with no named constant; 'failed twice' (main.rs:279-281) is the private `ATTEMPTS` (drain.rs:324) and is also a quoted report reason that tests/drain.rs:1124,1170,1683 assert; 'two thirds' (main.rs:72) is `rows.len() * 2 / 3` at labeled.rs:536, no constant; 'two separate git worktrees' (main.rs:176) describes a method, not a limit; `display.rs:705` ('one dispatch in three is Athena's own') is a report line of `athena plan`, not help text, and builds on a file outside the deliverables, so it is listed in D190's Tradeoff as a follow-up.
decisions.reason: A clap doc comment is a literal, so `format!` or `concat!` cannot take a constant there. D156's fill of `{ceiling}` (main.rs:605-623, tested by `drain_help_follows_the_ceiling_it_is_built_from`, main.rs:1511) is the existing, tested way. All values are already `pub`, so no file outside main.rs, lib.rs and the listed deliverables changes.

rejected.option: The `const_format` crate for `concat!`
rejected.why: It changes Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, which are not deliverables, and a derive doc comment cannot take it.

rejected.option: Convert only `plan`, `drain` and `check` (round 1)
rejected.why: It missed the Hestia review (already stale: 'urgent' against `BACKFILL_HIGH`, which makes causes high), the audience low rating and the rating range, which criterion 5 also covers.

rejected.option: Make `default_max_concurrency`, `ATTEMPTS` or the 30-second wait public so they can be read
rejected.why: It edits athena-data/config.rs and drain.rs, outside the listed files, and 'failed twice' is asserted as a report string. `Parallel::default()` already exposes the first.

rejected.option: Build the `display.rs:705` line from `IMPROVEMENT_GAP + 1` in this change
rejected.why: It is report output, not help, and adds another file outside the brief's list; stated as a follow-up in D190.

decisions.choice: Record as a new entry D190 (appended after D189 at decisions.md:5580, heading `## D190 · ` with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and a Provenance bullet). The Decision says `Amends D156` for the part it extends: D156's rule that help text states a limit from the constant that enforces it, now for more strings, and its alternative (d), a send-back of a finding inside the loop (decisions.md:4297-4300), now for stale text. It also adds one `[[link]]` older = D156, newer = D190, status = amended to docs/decision-links.toml. It states only what D187 already did: `decision_gate` 'already runs in the producer loop and again at the candidate' (decisions.md:5487, producer.rs:498). It does not claim to end D156's remark that the finding reaches the producer on the next attempt (decisions.md:4301-4304) for governed paths, and it names D187's open follow-ups (decisions.md:5506-5509) as untouched. No link to D187 is added. No existing entry is edited.
decisions.reason: A phrase `Amends D156` needs a matching link, or the gate holds the job (checks.rs:100-117 `link_problems`; `link_problem_sentence` at checks.rs:28-55). The log is append-only (mirrors.rs `decision log` AppendOnly) and `decision entries` needs the heading and a Provenance bullet (mirrors.rs:71-74). Saying the change 'ends' D156's tradeoff for the gate would itself put a false claim in the log (finding 6).

rejected.option: Write no phrase and add no link
rejected.why: The change extends D156 (help from constants, finding sent back in the loop). An entry that hides that leaves the log contradicting itself, which is what this check exists to stop.

rejected.option: Also link D187
rejected.why: This change does not finish any D187 follow-up (the advisory citation list for a passing change, the send-back intro, the briefs sentence); a link without a phrase fails `link_problems`.

decisions.choice: The check is not a reading check and adds no reading refusal. It does not enter `refusing_check`, which `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` reads (refusal_corpus.rs:2905). Its input forms are tested in stale_text.rs unit tests and the e2e tests. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is still run, as a regression demonstration that no reading outcome changed. Input forms and the test that covers each: a single number const; a single string const; a const with two literals (skipped); a const with no keyword after GENERIC words (skipped); `from 8 to 16` with a SCREAMING_SNAKE identifier; the same with a backticked identifier; the same with no identifier (not a needle); a quoted old claim after each marker; a quoted span under 6 words (not a claim); a cited `D<nn>` with and without a reversal word; a heading id absent from the log (ignored); a decision with each of the marking forms (a)-(c) and with a base-standing `amended` link; a claim wrapped over two lines; a deleted function and a deleted file; a moved comment; a CHANGELOG.md line; a line added by the diff.
decisions.reason: The task template asks for the input forms of any matching rule and their corpus cases. The corpus (refusal_corpus.rs:303-2760 case builders, `reading_check_cases` at :1993) exercises reading refusals only, so no existing case id maps to these forms. Adding corpus cases for a rule that never refuses a reading would test nothing.

rejected.option: Add refusal-corpus cases for the stale-text forms
rejected.why: The corpus runs `check_reading` over a stored reading; this rule runs over a diff and a tree and cannot produce a corpus outcome.

files.purpose: The pure check: `Hunk`, `Input`, `Stale` (Display `path:line (D<id>): still says <what> (<why>): <text>`), `STALE_REASON_PREFIX`, `MIN_CLAIM_WORDS`, `MAX_LISTED`; the needle extractors (const values from hunks, replaced-hunk claims, the reading's `from X to Y` with an identifier, quoted old claims, cited decision ids); the marked-entry rule with link status read by `toml_edit`; the search and the added-line exemption; `read_diff`, `read_files` and `check` (diff, needles, then the tree only when there are needles); and the unit tests for criteria 1-3.
Declare `mod stale_text;` and add the candidate-step block after the decision gate (after line 2020) that closes the job with the stale-text reason.
Call `stale_text_in_snapshot` in `producer_loop` beside the decision gate and add its findings to the all-clear test, the problem list, the limit-reached line and the send-back brief.
Add `Athena::stale_text_in_snapshot` and `Athena::stale_text_at_candidate`, the two adapters over `stale_text::check`; both take the accepted reading and print a skip line on a read error.
Add `append_stale_text` (leading sentence plus a `Stale text (fix each; the verifier runs after this):` section, a count of the rest, unchanged text for an empty list) with a unit test.
Add the three end-to-end `stale_text_*` tests (send-back then fix, unfixed ends before the verifier, reading-only) using `governed_job_with`, `editing`, `commit_file` and a reader wrapper script.
Add `fill_limits(command, &[(name, value)])`, which replaces `{name}` in about, long about, before/after help and each arg's help over the whole command tree, with a unit test.

Turn the literal limits in the `plan`, `drain`, `check`, `audience`, `drain-restart` and Hestia `review` help into placeholders filled in `cli_command()` from the enforcing constants; add `rating_parser()`; correct 'urgent' to 'high' in the Hestia help; add the help tests of criterion 5. Not in the brief's file list; criterion 5 asks for the diff of the file where each string lives (open question).
Append D190 (`Amends D156`) with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance; no existing entry is edited.
Add the `[[link]]` older D156, newer D190, status amended that the `Amends D156` phrase requires.
One `### Added` entry under `## [Unreleased]` stating what the diff does and nothing more.

steps: Write crates/athena-core/src/run/stale_text.rs. Types: `Hunk { path, removed, added }`, `Input { files, hunks, reading, base_headings, links }`, `Stale { path, line, decision, what, why, text }`, `Needles { values, claims, decisions }`. Functions: `needles(hunks, reading)` (const pairing by NAME within one path; replaced-hunk claims; reading `from X to Y` with an identifier, quoted old claims after the markers, cited `D<nn>` with a reversal word); `search(&Needles, &Input)` (whole-token value match with the keyword gate and the new-value skip; wrap-tolerant word-run claim match with line numbers; the added-line exemption; the marked rule (a)-(c) from decision 3 with `toml_edit` link statuses; the paragraph rule outside the log); `find(&Input)` (needles then search, for tests); `STALE_REASON_PREFIX = "stale text left by the change:"`; `MIN_CLAIM_WORDS = 6`; `MAX_LISTED = 30`.

In the same file write the git readers: `read_diff(git, from, to)` (parse `git diff -U0 --no-color --no-renames --no-ext-diff` into hunks per path, `+++ /dev/null` marking a deleted file), `read_files(git, tree)` (`ls_tree`, extension and size filters, CHANGELOG.md, `records/`, `target/`, `.git/` left out, `blob_sizes`, `cat_blobs` in chunks of 200) and `check(git, from, to, reading) -> Result<Vec<Stale>>` (diff, needles, return empty with no tree read when there are no needles, base headings from `show_file(from, "docs/decisions.md")`, links text from the searched files).

Write the stale_text.rs unit tests named in the demonstrations: the criterion 1 fixture and its no-keyword and two-literal cases; the criterion 2 decision fixture with its marked variants, the older-amendment case, 'amended by hand' (no id), and the three reading-only forms with a quiet variant; the criterion 3 fixtures after update, the added-line, marked-entry and CHANGELOG cases, the deleted-function, deleted-file and moved-comment cases, and `read_files` over a temporary git repository. Every test name contains `stale_text` through the module path so `cargo test -p athena-core stale_text` runs them.

Add `append_stale_text(text, &[Stale])` to send_back.rs (one leading sentence after `## Sent back`, then a `Stale text (fix each; the verifier runs after this):` section with one bullet per finding and a count of the rest) and a unit test that an empty list returns the text unchanged.

Add `Athena::stale_text_in_snapshot(&self, accepted, snapshot) -> Vec<Stale>` and `Athena::stale_text_at_candidate(&self, ctx, accepted, base, cand) -> Option<String>` to checks.rs. Both build the reading sentences (summary, assumptions, criteria; split at `. `, `; ` and newlines), call `stale_text::check` (loop: `snapshot.git()`, `snapshot.base()`, `snapshot.work_tree_tree()`; candidate: `self.git`, base and candidate commits), and on error print `producer   stale text not checked: <why>` and return empty or None.

Edit `producer_loop`: compute `stale` next to `gate` (skip when `self.nested.is_some()` or `changes.is_empty()`), add `stale.is_empty()` to the all-clear test at producer.rs:545, push `stale text left where the change makes it false: <n> place(s)` to `problems` after `report_problems` is cloned, print `producer   stale text still left after the send-back; the job ends before the verifier` in the limit branch, and wrap the `attempt_brief` expression in `append_stale_text` last. Add `mod stale_text;` to run/mod.rs and the candidate block after mod.rs:2020 with the same guards and the `changed_paths` / `verification_passed = None` handling as mod.rs:2013-2019.

Add the three end-to-end tests to run/tests.rs: `stale_text_is_sent_back_to_the_producer_before_verification` (with the fix on send-back, which is also the criterion 3 landing test), `stale_text_left_after_the_send_back_ends_the_job_before_the_verifier`, and `stale_text_from_the_reading_alone_is_sent_back_and_fixed` (a reader wrapper script that sets `reading["summary"]`, as tests.rs:1381-1385 does). Seed `src/limits.rs` and `HELP.md` with `commit_file`.

In athena-cli add `fill_limits` to lib.rs with its unit test. risks.risk: False positives: an unrelated line holds the old number, or a replaced line's words survive in a document. A hard failure at the candidate then forces a producer to write an 'Amends Dn in prose only' entry for an old decision it did not change.
risks.mitigation: Value hits need a shared name keyword plus the old value as a whole token, and skip lines that also hold the new value. Claims come only from replaced hunks, need 6 or more words, a comment or prose line, a whole-line word run, and must not be re-added. Reading values need a named identifier. A decision cited from the reading needs a reversal word. Output is capped at 30 findings plus a count. The finding text names the escape (`Amends D<n> in prose only` with an `amended` link, the convention of checks.rs:94-97). Tests cover a non-matching 8, a moved comment, a deleted function and a deleted file. The refusal rate is the brief's estimate, not measured.

risks.risk: Reading every text file of the tree on each producer pass costs time and memory on a large repository.
risks.mitigation: The tree is read only when the diff or reading yields a needle. Only `.rs .md .toml .yml .yaml .sh` files of at most 2 MiB are read; CHANGELOG.md, `records/`, `target/` and `.git/` are skipped; blobs are read in chunks of 200 with one `cat-file --batch` (`cat_blobs`, athena-git lib.rs:988) after `blob_sizes` (:966). A failed read is a skip line, not a failure.

risks.risk: A decision that restates the old rule in other words is missed, and the reading forms miss a rule the reader wrote in other words. A heading that moves is re-keyed by id, not line.
risks.mitigation: The brief puts semantic matching out of scope. The wrap-tolerant word-run match and the entry/paragraph rule are covered by tests with a wrapped sentence and with the marking forms. D190's Tradeoff says reworded reversals are not caught.

risks.risk: The new decision entry or the CHANGELOG entry trips the ontology rule, the append-only rule or the banned-word scan.
risks.mitigation: The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core mirrors`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` and `cargo test -p xtask` after writing D190. D190 contains no ontology term definition and is appended at the end of the file.

risks.risk: A clap doc comment is stored as `about` or `long_about` depending on its paragraphs, and an arg's text as `help` or `long_help`, so a fill that reads the wrong getter leaves a placeholder in the help.
risks.mitigation: `fill_limits` fills whichever of about, long about, before/after help and each arg's help or long help exists, over every subcommand, and the criterion 5 test asserts no `{` survives in the rendered help of each converted command. clap is 4.6.7 (Cargo.lock:249-251); if `mut_subcommands` or `mut_args` is missing, use `mut_subcommand` per name. If `jiff::SignedDuration::as_mins` is missing, use `as_secs() / 60` for `PENDING_WINDOW`.

risks.risk: A retry brief omits the stale-text finding because `retry_findings` (retry.rs:476-500) is not extended.
risks.mitigation: The retry's own producer loop reruns the check and supplies the list in its first send-back (shown by the loop test); stated in D190's Tradeoff.

risks.risk: The producer's own change trips the check on this job's own diff (for example a real copy of a replaced help line in docs).
risks.mitigation: Only whole replaced lines of 6 or more words are needles, and this job's reading holds no `from X to Y` beside an identifier. If the send-back lists a real stale place outside the listed files, the producer reports it as an open issue and does not widen scope, since criterion 9 forbids other files.

demonstrations.method: Run the three recorded checks on the final tree: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`. Also `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` (the reading corpus must be unchanged because no reading code is touched), `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo test -p xtask`. I have not run them and cite no result.
demonstrations.fails_without: Any existing test that the new check or the help change breaks fails the run: the run tests that drive `producer_loop` and `check_and_verify` (the `governed_edit_*` tests, tests.rs:3636-3779; `settle_loop_checks`, tests.rs:6252), the pin tests in run_pin_tests.rs, the help tests in main.rs and tests/drain.rs. The existing run tests change the README to short text and have no changed constant, no 6-word replaced line and no identifier in the reading, so they must stay unchanged.
demonstrations.seam: The real test suite and the existing fake-agent harness (tests.rs:180-285).

demonstrations.method: `git status` and `git diff --stat` list only: run/stale_text.rs, run/mod.rs, run/producer.rs, run/checks.rs, run/send_back.rs, run/tests.rs, athena-cli lib.rs and main.rs, docs/decisions.md, docs/decision-links.toml and CHANGELOG.md. No athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, Cargo file, drain.rs, display.rs, hestia.rs or athena-data file changes, since every constant used is already `pub`. Without a changed constant, a replaced claim or a reading form, the check returns nothing; the unchanged existing run tests show it.
